leagues.after: no final; 8th played a relegation play-off (16 May 2026), 9th-10th relegated directly
leagues.quote: The four teams that qualified to the final four round played an additional round between each other. Their points were halved, rounded downwards. All matches were played in Arena Kombetare, which serves as a neutral ground.
leagues.note: 2025-26, 10 clubs, no championship/relegation groups: one 36-round table (four meetings), then only the top four play a 3-round mini-league for the title. Points are halved and rounded down, goals are not carried. Egnatia won the title in the last match on 31 May 2026 (season window 22 Aug 2025 - 31 May 2026); the last regular matchday is not dated on the article.

leagues.after: promotion play-offs 3rd-6th (single-leg semis 7 May, final 11 May 2026); their winner met the 8th-placed Superiore club (16 May). Relegation play-outs for 9th-10th, 11th-12th relegated
leagues.quote: The season began on 23 August 2025 and ended on 4 May 2026. There were 12 teams competing this season. The winning and runner-up teams gained promotion to the 2026–27 Kategoria Superiore. The promotion play-offs winner played a promotion play-off match against the 8th ranked team of the 2025–26 Kategoria Superiore.
leagues.note: Not split. One table over 33 rounds: the results are published as 'Rounds 1-22' and 'Rounds 23-33' (12 clubs, so 22 + 11 = 33 matches each); the fixture list is titled '33 weeks of football'. Places 1-2 promoted, 3-6 play off, 9-10 play out, 11-12 relegated.

leagues.after: no final; bottom 3 of the relegation group relegated
leagues.quote: 14 teams participate in the league. In the first round, known as Regular Season, all teams play each other home and away, for a total of 26 games each. In the second round, the league splits into two groups: Teams ranked 1–6 enter the Championship Playoffs, whereas teams ranked 7–14 enter the Relegation playoffs. The teams in the Championship Playoffs play each other home and away for an additional 10 games each, while the teams in the Relegation Playoffs play each other only once, either home or away, for an additional 7 games each. All criteria (such as points, goal difference, and head to head records) are retained during the transition from first to second round. The team ranked first in the Championship Playoffs are declared champions, while the bottom three teams in the Relegation Playoffs are relegated to the Second Division.
leagues.note: 2025-26: 22 Aug 2025 - 22 May 2026. Championship group totals 36 matches, relegation group 33; top 4 of the championship group take the European places. The first split matchday is not dated on the article.

leagues.after: no final; top 3 of the Promotion Round promoted, bottom 3 of the Relegation Round relegated
leagues.quote: During the regular season, each team faced each other once (either at home or away). Afterwards, the table split into two groups, with the top eight teams entering the Promotion Round and the bottom eight teams entering the Relegation Round.
leagues.note: 2025-26, 16 clubs, 12 Sep 2025 - 25 Apr 2026. Regular season is a single round-robin (15 matches); each group then plays home and away (14 more, 29 total). 'Results from the regular season were carried over into this round' - the tables carry the Phase I points as opening points (adjust_points of 41/29/24/26 for the top four).

leagues.after: Final Four of the round winners/runners-up: two single-leg semi-finals, third-place match and final (16 May 2026); no two-legged ties
leagues.quote: The Opening Round will see each of the 12 teams play each other once before the league is then split between a Top 6 and a Bottom 6, allowing for the teams in each of those splits to play each other another time. Once the ranking is set, each team will go back down to 0 points and start from scratch in the Closing Round, where the same process will be repeated.
leagues.note: 2025-26 is a double competition, not one long split: Opening Round (11 rounds + 5 in the split, points kept in full) then a full reset to 0 for an identical Closing Round. The id 'Opening Round' is one of those two rounds. Title: the same club winning both rounds is champion; otherwise a Final Four of both rounds' winners and runners-up (seeded on aggregate points) decides it - 2025-26 Floriana won the final on 16 May 2026. Season window 16 Aug 2025 - 16 May 2026. The first split matchday is not dated on the article.

leagues.after: no final; champion and runner-up promoted, a tie-break play-off decided 2nd promotion (23 Apr 2026); bottom two relegated
leagues.quote: During the regular season, each team plays each other once (either at home or at away). The top eight teams qualify for the Top eight, while the bottom eight teams qualify for the Play-Out.
leagues.note: 2025-26, 16 clubs, 13 Sep 2025 - 23 Apr 2026; 15 rounds single round-robin, then 8+8 groups of one more round-robin (7 more, 22 total). The article prints one cumulative table (every club Pld 22) and states no halving rule, so full carry is inferred from the table rather than quoted.

leagues.after: no final; top 2 promoted, bottom 4 relegated (a 9 May 2026 play-off broke the tie for 10th/11th and the last relegation place)
leagues.quote: During the regular season, each team plays each other twice in a round robin format. The top two teams will be promoted to the Challenge League for the following season, while the bottom four teams will be relegated to the National Amateur League II.
leagues.note: Third tier, not split: 14 clubs, one 26-round table, 19 Sep 2025 - 11 May 2026 (table complete 29 Apr, tie-break play-off 9 May). National League I 2026-27 keeps the single round-robin table (18 Sep 2026 - 11 May 2027).

leagues.after: no final; bottom 2 of the relegation play-outs relegated
leagues.quote: The top four teams from the regular season met twice (6 matches per team) for places in the 2026–27 UEFA Champions League, 2026–27 UEFA Europa League and 2026–27 UEFA Conference League as well as deciding the League Champion. Points and goals were carried over in full from the regular season. [...] The teams met twice (6 matches per team) and entered this round with half the points they earned during the regular season.
leagues.note: 2025-26: three groups, not the old 6/8. 14 clubs, 26 rounds (23 Aug 2025 - 22 Mar 2026, winter break from 22 Dec 2025), then 4 Apr - 21 May 2026. Points: championship group full (goals too), Europe group half; the article states no rule for the 6-team relegation play-outs, so that value is genuinely unknown (marked mixed). 2026-27 repeats the same 4/4/6 split.

leagues.after: no final; top 2 promoted, bottom 4 relegated
leagues.quote: The championship is being held with 16 teams in one group in one phase, where each team will face all opponents twice home and away, a total of 30 matches in the unified Group, after the further reduction of the teams from last year without play-offs for the promotion and play-outs for the relegation.
leagues.note: Not split in 2026-27. The split existed in 2025-26 only: 20 clubs in two groups of 10 (18 rounds, from 13 Sep 2025), then play-offs for 1st-4th of each group (6 rounds) and play-outs for 5th-10th (10 rounds), both starting with half the Phase I points, 15 Feb - 26 Apr 2026.

leagues.after: no final; bottom 2 of the relegation round relegated
leagues.quote: Teams play each other once for the third time (either at home or away) for a total of 5 games each.
leagues.note: 2026: 12 clubs, 10 Apr - 24 Oct 2026; top 6 / bottom 6 after 22 rounds, 5 more matches each (27 total). The article only spells out the extra 5 games; full points carry is read off the cumulative tables (Pld 27), not quoted. The first split matchday is not dated.

leagues.after: single-match promotion play-offs among 2nd-5th; champion promoted directly
leagues.quote: Each team plays each other twice (22 matches each), once at home and once away. [...] Teams placed 2nd-5th qualified for the 1. deild karla play-offs, with the winners earning promotion to the 2026 Besta deild karla.
leagues.note: Not split: 12 clubs, one 22-round table. Dates are the 2025 season (2 May - 13 Sep 2025) - no 2026 season article exists, and 2026 promotion was decided the same way (champions Þór Akureyri + play-off winners Keflavík).

leagues.after: no final; promotion/relegation straight from the table
leagues.quote: Each team plays each other twice (22 matches each), once at home and once away.
leagues.note: Third tier, not split: 12 clubs, one 22-round table. The 2025 article carries no season dates and no 2026 article exists; no promotion play-off is described.

leagues.after: two-legged play-off: 11th vs Ykkösliiga 2nd (2026: FF Jaro v PK-35); 12th relegated
leagues.quote: The eleventh-placed team (FF Jaro) faced the second-placed team of the 2026 Ykkösliiga (PK-35) in a two-legged play-off for the final place in the 2027 [Veikkausliiga].
leagues.note: 2026: 12 clubs, 4 Apr - 1 Nov 2026; top 6 / bottom 6 after 22 rounds. The group size and rounds are derived from the tables (Oulu Pld 22 in the regular season, Pld 32 in the championship round = 10 more, i.e. a double round-robin inside each group), not from a quoted sentence.

leagues.after: two-legged play-off: 9th vs Ykkönen 2nd (2026: KäPa v RoPS); champion promoted, last relegated
leagues.quote: Teams play each other three times in a triple round-robin format, for a total of 27 matches.
leagues.note: Not split: 10 clubs, one 27-round table, 3 Apr - 17 Oct 2026. The ninth-placed club plays the Ykkönen runner-up in a two-legged play-off.

leagues.after: winner promoted directly; runner-up plays a two-legged tie vs the 9th-placed Ykkösliiga club
leagues.quote: The top six teams from the regular season enter the Promotion Round, where they play each other once more. Points from the regular season are carried over. The winner is promoted directly to the Ykkösliiga, while the runners-up advance to a two-legged playoff against the ninth-placed team of the Ykkösliiga.
leagues.note: 2026: 12 clubs, 2 Apr - 18 Oct 2026; 22 rounds regular (table), 5 more in each group (27 total); bottom six play a Relegation Round, also carrying points.

leagues.after: no final; group winner promoted or enters the promotion play-offs, bottom two normally relegated
leagues.quote: There are 110 clubs in the Kolmonen, divided in 10 groups of 8 to 12 teams each representing a geographical area. The top team in each Kolmonen group are either promoted to Kakkonen or go to promotion play-offs with six teams in total getting promoted, and the two lowest placed teams are normally relegated to the Nelonen.
leagues.note: Fourth tier, regional - never split and no season article. The 2026 club list gives 12 clubs in South Group B, so 22 rounds of a double round-robin is derived from the group size, not quoted; no 2026 dates are published for this group.

leagues.after: no final; 7th-8th of Phase I drop out of the title race (2025-26: Spartanii Sportul relegated)
leagues.quote: Points gained between the top 6 teams in Phase I are halved, rounded downwards, and no other records are carried over.
leagues.note: 8 clubs, 14 rounds in Phase I (double round-robin), then only the top six continue: 10 more matches (double round-robin of six). Halved and rounded-down points, goal records reset. The 2026-27 article repeats the identical rule ('15 games for each team will count for Phase II' is stale boilerplate there). Season dates are not in either infobox; the cup/league calendar is Jul-May.

leagues.after: promotion decided by a knockout play-off bracket (4 single-leg rounds, 6-27 May) on top of the league places
leagues.quote: The season started on 25 July 2025 and concluded on 9 May 2026, with play-off matches played between 6 and 27 May for a place in Moldovan Liga next season.
leagues.note: Not a single-table split: Phase I is itself two groups (the 2025-26 tables show 15 matches each, i.e. triple round-robin in groups of six), then Phase II regroups everyone by ranking into a 6-club Group 1 (10 matches) and an 8-club Group 2 (7 matches). The article states no points-carry rule, hence unknown. 14 clubs in 2025-26; promoted: Politehnica UTM and Real Sireți.
